29.16.7.en: * Who can contemplate in quietness, perceiving the glory of the divine majesty, during this work? For he is "he that delivereth the poor from him that is too strong for him, yea, the poor and the needy from him that spoileth him" (Ps 35:10), "I brake the jaws of the wicked, and plucked the spoil out of his teeth" (Job 29:17). Who, while caring for the poor... is able to contemplate the greatness of blessedness, and while he is occupied with the needs of the present life for their sake, to have his heart always lifted above the filth of the earth?!... Which of men, even if he were the chief of the righteous saints, do we think could at any time, while bound by the fetters of this life, reach this chief good without ceasing from holy contemplation? Is he not drawn away, if only for a short time, from Him who alone is good by earthly thoughts? Does he not care, if only for a while, about food or clothing or other bodily matters, or about receiving the brethren, or changing his place, or building his cell...?

29.17.s.en: 4. His hopes for the continuance of his happiness

29.17.0.en: 18 "Then I said, I shall die in my nest, and I shall multiply my days as the salamander. 19 My root was spread out by the waters, and the dew lay all night upon my branch. 20 My glory was fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand. 21 Unto me men gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel. 22 After my words they spake not again; and my speech dropped upon them. 23 And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain. 24 If I laughed on them, they believed it not; and the light of my countenance they cast not down. 25 I chose out their way, and sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners.

29.17.1.en: "Then I said, I shall die in my nest, and I shall multiply my days as the salamander" [18].

29.17.2.en: Job counted himself in a nest to which he flees and where he dwells securely, or a nest in which he settles as at the top of a tree, safe from any dangers that might befall him until the moment comes to give up his spirit. He thought that he would spend all his days in peace, far from any storms that could shatter his nest or shake his lodging.

29.17.3.en: It is wondrous that Job looks at his life as being like the sand (the salamander) that is on the seashore, as though he thought his life would be very long, and did not realize that it is like the grains of sand that fall from the hourglass and run out in a short time.

29.17.4.en: * "And I said, I shall die in my nest, and like the palm tree I shall multiply my days" [18]... The likening of the life of the righteous to the palm tree is fitting, because the palm tree is rough to the touch below, and in a way is wrapped in dry bark, but above it bears fruit. Below it is compressed by its spread-out bark, but above it is spread out with great greenness. So is the life of the chosen, despised below, and beautiful on high...

29.18.0.en: "My root was spread out by the waters, and the dew lay all night upon my branch" [19].

29.18.1.en: Job considered himself like a tree planted by the streams of water, always watered, which makes it fruitful and flourishing, so that it never withers.

29.18.2.en: [The dew lay all night upon his branch]: if Job was planted like a tree enjoying the richness of the earth, he receives the blessings of heaven as dew. He is the delight of God who cares for him.

29.18.3.en: * "My roots are open to the waters" [19], when the thought of the mind spreads secretly to receive the streams of truth. In Holy Scripture roots point to hidden thought. Therefore we open our roots to the waters when we spread the hidden thought of our heart to the inner waters...

29.18.4.en: The Psalmist says: "He shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water" (Ps 1:3)...

29.18.5.en: ["And the dew lay all night upon my harvest"]... The dew falls from above, but the harvest is gathered from below. So the dew rests upon the harvest, for the grace that comes down from on high makes us persons fit to be gathered in the world from below. By the same grace that waters us from above we bear the fruit of good work. So Paul rightly says: "But by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace which was bestowed upon me was not in vain" (1 Cor 15:10)... As we look at the harvest growing under the dew, we hear him say: "His grace which was bestowed upon me was not in vain; but I laboured more abundantly than they all" (1 Cor 15:10).

29.19.0.en: "My glory was fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand" [20].

29.19.1.en: With every new day he carried a new thought in the life of righteousness, for he loved love and tenderness; therefore his honor did not grow old. He says, "My glory was fresh in me"; it will never wither. He does not grow weary of striving with all his strength for the oppressed, for he says, "My bow was renewed in my hand."

29.19.2.en: * "My glory was fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand" [20]... All who know what is true realize that oldness (aging) is usually among the marks of evil, while newness is among the marks of virtue. Therefore Paul says: "Seeing that ye have put off the old man with his deeds; and have put on the new man" (Col 3:9-10)... As for our zeal (enthusiasm), when we are among our spiritual enemies or among our various kinsmen in the flesh, we are to some extent absorbed in their habits and so grow old, and we defile the form of our newness which we received through prayer and reading and the good life, through earnest sufferings and daily vigil, yet in our old age we are renewed and refreshed. So when our life is washed with tears, practices good works, and is filled with holy meditations, it recovers its newness without ceasing...

29.19.3.en: The "bow" in the Holy Scriptures sometimes points to the plans of the wicked, as when it says: "[They] bend their bows to shoot their arrows, even bitter words" (Ps 64:3). The same Psalmist referred to the day of judgment: "Thou hast shewed thy people hard things: thou hast made us to drink the wine of astonishment. Thou hast given a banner to them that fear thee, that it may be displayed because of the truth, that they may flee from the bow" (Ps 60:3-4)...

29.19.4.en: Sometimes the bow is used in Holy Scripture for good things. This one is of the bow of the Church, and that one of the bow of the Lord, from which the arrows, the terrifying words, go out to the hearts of men. The Psalmist rightly said: "He hath bent his bow, and made it ready. He hath also prepared for him the instruments of death; he ordaineth his arrows against the persecutors" (Ps 7:12-13)...

29.19.5.en: The bow in the hand is Holy Scripture in action. He holds a bow in his hand who practices in deed the divine declarations that he has learned with understanding. So [the bow is renewed in the hand] in that all we learn concerning the holy declaration by study is accomplished by practicing it in deed...

29.19.6.en: The blessed David tells us of his circumstances, and foretells our circumstances, and while he points to his sorrows, he speaks equally of what concerns the holy Church and her circumstances in the same sense.

29.20.0.en: "Unto me men gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel" [21].

29.20.1.en: Since his fatherhood to the poor was blended with courage and struggle for the oppressed, together with wisdom and dignity, he became the foremost counselor; when he spoke, all fell silent and listened to him, knowing that nothing could be found fault with in him and nothing was lacking in him.

29.20.2.en: * ["They that heard me waited for my judgment, and they that listened were silent at my counsel"]... We miss this reverence which those under him offer; it is directed toward the blessed Job. The holy Church also, who suffers bitterly from heretics or from the carnal, remembers the former days too, when all the faithful with whom she spoke listened to her with fear. She laments the boldness of those who oppose her, and says: [They that heard me waited for my judgment, and they that listened were silent at my counsel].

29.21.0.en: "After my words they spake not again; and my speech dropped upon them" [22].

29.21.1.en: When he spoke, everyone felt there was no further need to inquire into the matter, for Job was distinguished by the precision with which he examined things. Therefore there was no one to speak again after his words or to add anything to them.

29.21.2.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) comments on the saying of the blessed Job, ["And to my words they added nothing"], by saying that the faithful did not dare to add anything of their own to the words of the holy Church, as the heretics did, who dared to add something to her words, as though they were busy correcting the uprightness of the Church's teachings and preaching.

29.22.0.en: "And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain" [23].

29.22.1.en: All were like a wasteland in need of rain falling from Job's lips, that their wilderness might be turned into a fruitful garden. They were a land thirsty for rain. All realized the value of the wisdom coming out of his mouth; they waited for it and drank it in, so that it might bear fruit within them as in their outward conduct.

29.22.2.en: * "And they waited for me as for the rain, and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain" [23]. We submit to the words of holy preaching like rain when, in true humility, we recognize the dryness of our hearts and long to drink the draughts of holy preaching. Rightly it is said to God by the Psalmist: ["My soul thirsteth after thee, as a thirsty land"] (Ps 143:6). The prophet commands us to be refreshed by the streams of teaching, saying: "Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters" (Isa 55:1).

29.23.0.en: "If I laughed on them, they believed it not; and the light of my countenance they cast not down" [24].

29.23.1.en: When he smiled at someone, that person was in surpassing happiness, so that he thought he was as in a dream. All sought his favor and pleasure, for he put aside formality, smiling and laughing. He gave those around him an atmosphere of warmth and joy. Those present did not abuse his simplicity, nor did they lessen their respect for him, but looked to the radiance of his face with rejoicing, without frowning.

29.23.2.en: * "If I laughed on them, they believed it not; and the light of my countenance did not fall to the ground" [24]. If we understand this through the historical interpretation, we should imagine that the holy man shows himself in a certain way to those under him, that even in his laughter he is able to be awe-inspiring. He related that he was a father to the poor, and a comforter to widows. This matter needs great discernment, how, with this firmness in action, he also shows such great kindness and tender sympathy in it...

29.23.3.en: So we should learn here that a man should govern himself in his relation to others by the following measure: that when he laughs he should be dignified, and when he is angry he should be lovable. In his excessive merriment he should not be trifling, and his anger should not be without limit, making him hated. We often crush those under our care when we exaggerate the keeping of justice beyond its bounds. Then it is not justice. It does not keep itself under such exaggerated discipline...

29.23.4.en: Let us see how Paul bears a smile through the grace from on high... even in the midst of his fears and afflictions... He was caught up to the third heaven above him, and carried into Paradise, where he heard unspeakable words (2 Cor 12:2). And yet he remained fearful, for he says: "But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway" (1 Cor 9:27). You see how, when divine grace smiles upon him, he is filled with assurance and hope, and yet does not trust in relying on himself.

29.24.0.en: "I chose out their way, and sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners" [25].

29.24.1.en: In simplicity he smiles with dignity to pour out the spirit of cheerfulness upon those present, and at the same time he does not abandon steering the ship of their lives, for he is the captain of the ship. "I chose out their way, and sat chief."

29.24.2.en: His smile does not remove his awe as a king and a commander in battle: "And dwelt as a king in the army." When he gave a command, all obeyed him as soldiers obey the commander of the army. He says to this one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to his servant, Do this, and he doeth it" (Mt 8:9).

29.24.3.en: His leadership does not cause distress or resentment, for he does not love authority; he leads only to comfort the mourners by the tenderness of his heart and his support for all in the truth mingled with love.

29.24.4.en: * [I chose out their way, and sat chief (head)] [25]. In the hearts of perishing sinners the works of the flesh hold the first place, and the works of the soul the next place. Certainly in their thoughts Christ does not sit first, but holds the last place. But the chosen man cares for eternal things above everything. If there is a temporal matter, he manages it as a secondary matter, and it holds less of his attention. The voice of Truth says: "But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you" (Mt 6:33)...

29.24.5.en: ["When I sat as a king surrounded by an army, yet I was a comforter of the mourners."] The Lord sits as a king in the heart, for He rules the noisy emotions of the heart in our thoughts. In the soul in which He dwells He gives zeal to the sluggish, restrains the restless, inflames the cold, tempers the fiery, softens the hard, and binds the dissolute, so that by this variety of thoughts He is surrounded by a kind of army. Or certainly He sits as a king surrounded by an army, because that King rules over the minds of the chosen in the midst of a host of virtues.

29.24.6.en: He is also [the comforter of the mourners], through the promise He gave, saying: "Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted" (Mt 5:4). Again: "But I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you" (Jn 16:22)...

29.24.7.en: The hearts of the mourners are also comforted by the holy Church, as she guides the souls of the chosen. She is weighed down by the woes of the present journey, and gladdens them with the promise of the eternal city...

29.24.8.en: The holy Church mingles hope and fear together for those who believe in her, so that they come into contact with the tenderness and justice of the Saviour in her continual service. She does this so that they may not rely on mercy and become lax, nor lose hope through terror of justice. So she gladdens those who are warned by the words of her Head, saying: "Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom" (Lk 12:32). Likewise she warns the presumptuous: "Watch ye and pray, lest ye enter into temptation" (Mk 14:38). And she gladdens those in terror, saying: "Rejoice, because your names are written in heaven" (Lk 10:20). But those who rely on themselves she terrifies, saying: ["I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven"].

29.24.9.en: She gladdens those in terror, saying: "My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: and I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand" (Jn 10:27-28)...

29.24.10.en: * Tenderness is mingled with severity (firmness)... This truly appears in the ark of the covenant, where the rod and the manna are found together beside the tables of the Law, there where the knowledge of Holy Scripture is in the breast of the good ruler, with the rod of severity (firmness), let there be sweetness too. So David says: "Thy rod and thy staff they comfort me" (Ps 23:4).

29.24.12.en: * Just as a sick man who is concerned for the healing of his body accepts with full willingness every remedy the physician prescribes for him, even if it is very bitter, and in this he does not complain or become distressed, nor does he suspect ill intent in the physician, so it is with the humble man who desires his spiritual growth. He accepts with full willingness the reproofs and counsels of the superior, without imagining that the superior does this out of hatred and harshness.

29.24.13.en: If for bodily healing we accept bitter, loathsome medicines, and risk the cutting off of limbs and cauterization by fire, and in this we thank the physicians and surgeons who care for us despite the painful treatments, how much more does right reason call us to do this for the salvation of our souls, even if the remedy, counsel and reproof, is bitter?!

29.24.14.en: St. Basil the Great * (Laxity toward sinners) is not virtue but weakness. Nor is it love or meekness but neglect; indeed it is cruelty toward those souls that are overlooked, and perish without being warned of their ruin.

29.24.15.en: St. Augustine * He who shepherds the sheep should be neither a lion nor a ewe.

29.24.17.en: Your care for me is the subject of my praise!

29.24.18.en: * I look to the past, and I touch Your hand that has kept me.

29.24.19.en: If there is any goodness in me, it is from the riches of Your grace upon me!

29.24.20.en: * You counted me as a lighthouse, and Your lamp shone upon my head.

29.24.22.en: Your word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light to my mind.

29.24.23.en: You set me up as a lighthouse to bear Your light.

29.24.24.en: I bear witness to Your care, and so You draw many to You through me.

29.24.25.en: * You have blessed my nature in Yourself, You who became incarnate for me.

29.24.26.en: Let me stand in amazement before Your love, You who sit with me in my tent.

29.24.27.en: * I stand in the midst of my family, and I see You blessing us at once.

29.24.28.en: How my soul longs to stand with all mankind, and to see You revealed with Your love and care in the midst of all!

29.24.29.en: * By Your care You give us everything in abundance, for with You present with us nothing is lacking to us.

29.24.30.en: You cleanse us and wash us as with milk, and You cause streams of oil to overflow from the rocks!

29.24.31.en: * I am satisfied in You, and so I long to serve all!

29.24.32.en: I seek not what is for myself, nor what is for my honor, but what is for Your beloved ones!

29.24.33.en: * Your care for the Church is surpassing!

29.24.34.en: You give her Your wisdom, so she speaks Your words and bears Your wondrous thought!

29.24.35.en: You judge among men, not as one who condemns, but as one who supports and shows compassion.

29.24.36.en: You give her honor, not that she may exalt herself, but that she may bow down and wash feet.

29.24.37.en: * In Your care You allow even heretics their full freedom.

29.24.38.en: They trouble Your Church, but in the midst of affliction she enjoys heavenly blessedness.

29.24.39.en: And in the midst of opposition she draws many to Your heavens!

29.24.40.en: You are the Good One who brings forth food out of the eater, and from evils You raise up what is for the edification of many.

29.24.41.en: * You stretched out Your arms to me, the orphan!

29.24.42.en: And the Father became a Father to me, so my orphanhood was transformed by the surpassing practical sonship.

29.24.43.en: Grant me to have compassion on every orphan; when shall I see all mankind enjoying practical sonship to God?!

29.24.44.en: * When shall we return the souls that have become orphans to their heavenly Father, and so enjoy their blessings upon us?

29.24.45.en: * Grant me to be covered by Your righteousness, so that I do not cease giving.

29.24.46.en: Grant me to be adorned with Your crown: that is, with righteousness and mercy!

29.24.47.en: Your righteousness has become the subject of my sweetness; I acquire it, and so I show compassion to every human being!

29.24.48.en: Let the world take its garment from me, as the Egyptian woman did with righteous Joseph, but do not allow the devil to strip off Your garment that You gave me!

29.24.49.en: It is not his right to seize it as long as I cherish it!

29.24.50.en: * Grant that Your righteousness may cover my whole being, and that the enemy of good may have no way into my depths!

29.24.51.en: He will find in me no breach as long as I am kept by Your righteousness.

29.24.52.en: * Grant me by Your grace to become eyes to the blind.

29.24.53.en: You enlighten me, and make of me a light for others.

29.24.54.en: You remove my darkness, and in You I support those who sit in darkness.

29.24.55.en: * Grant me the spirit of tender fatherhood, O Father of all mankind.

29.24.56.en: That I may have compassion on all, and care, if possible, for everyone!

29.24.57.en: * Grant me Your grace from above like the dew, and water my life on earth with the waters of Your Holy Spirit.

29.24.58.en: So that my spiritual youth may be renewed like the eagle's, and my soul may not grow old with a spirit of helplessness and weakness.

29.24.59.en: * Grant me, O Lord, to walk in the Spirit.

29.24.60.en: If I rejoice and laugh, may I carry the spirit of firmness.

29.24.61.en: And if I become firm, may I carry the spirit of tenderness.

29.24.62.en: May my merriment be completed by my firmness, and my firmness be completed by my tenderness!

29.24.63.en: * Grant me the spirit of cheerfulness, so that in You I may be a source of joy.

29.24.64.en: And in my cheerfulness I will not be slack in working earnestly.

29.24.65.en: Grant me the spirit of leadership without arrogance, so that I work not in a spirit of domination, but in a spirit of fatherhood!

29.24.66.en: I support all, so that they may bear the spirit of earnest leadership!
